title: Knowledge Retrieval / Knowledge Router mislabeled as built-in agents
reality: In v2.3.0 optional agents moved out of the base Engine into downloadable packages (base Engine shrank by 25,000+ lines; fresh installs contain no optional agents). The Marinara-Agents catalog (github.com/Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents, 29 first-party packages) lists Knowledge Retrieval (`knowledge-retrieval`) and Knowledge Router (`knowledge-router`) as downloadable Writer Agent packages installed via Agents → Download Agents. Existing installs migrate their agents automatically; official packages also auto-update from the version-matched catalog lane at startup (v2.3.1, #3712 in 2.3.3).
fix: In the 'Knowledge Retrieval, Router & Sources' section of references/lorebooks.md, change '`knowledge-retrieval` built-in agent' and '`knowledge-router` built-in agent' to downloadable Writer Agent packages from the official Marinara-Agents catalog (Agents → Download Agents). Add that fresh v2.3+ installs include NO optional agents, so semantic lorebook retrieval requires installing the package first; upgrades from ≤2.2 migrate installed agents and settings automatically.

title: Lorebook Keeper is now a downloadable agent package
reality: As of v2.3.0 Lorebook Keeper is a downloadable Misc Agent package (`lorebook-keeper`) in the Marinara-Agents catalog, not built into the Engine; Game setup only shows its controls when the package is installed (2.3.0 fixed list). Fresh installs do not have it.
fix: references/lorebooks.md references Lorebook Keeper in the `locked` field row and the v2.1 entry-length note as if always present. Add a v2.3 note that Lorebook Keeper is now the `lorebook-keeper` downloadable Misc Agent package installed via Agents → Download Agents; guidance about it only applies when installed.

title: Missing v2.3.0 semantic-similarity baseline calibration
reality: v2.3.0 (#3627) calibrated Lorebook semantic similarity against an unrelated-text baseline, so embedding models whose raw cosine scores cluster around 0.97 no longer inject unrelated entries at every usable threshold or suppress relevant entries near 1.0.
fix: In the 'Knowledge Retrieval, Router & Sources (Semantic Matching)' section (near the v2.2 vector-fallback paragraph), add a v2.3.0 note: similarity scores are now calibrated against an unrelated-text baseline before threshold comparison, making score thresholds meaningful even with embedding models that produce tightly clustered raw cosine scores; users no longer need to hand-tune extreme thresholds for such models (#3627).

title: Noodle lorebook context budget is now a fixed 8,192 tokens
reality: v2.3.2 changed Noodle refreshes so world/lore context and chat carryover each get a fixed 8,192-token budget, so large invited rosters cannot inflate generations. The skill says the Noodle lorebook context uses 'a Noodle-specific token budget that scales with active character count'.
fix: In the Scope section's '(v2.2)' Noodle paragraph, replace 'a Noodle-specific token budget that scales with active character count' with the v2.3.2 behavior: world/lore context has a fixed 8,192-token budget in Noodle refreshes (chat carryover has its own separate 8,192-token budget), independent of roster size. Also note (v2.3.2, #3687) that active Persona, Character, and linked-lorebook macros are resolved before Noodle refresh prompts reach the model.

title: Missing macro resolution through lorebook routing and embedding scans
reality: v2.3.2 (#3704) resolves {{user}}, {{char}}, and other prompt macros at the final provider boundary, explicitly including lorebook routing and embedding scans, so late prompt injections (opening greetings, /guided instructions) can no longer reach lorebook keyword/semantic matching or the model with raw identity placeholders.
fix: Add a note in references/lorebooks.md (Keyword choice best practices and/or the Semantic Matching section): as of v2.3.2, macros are resolved before lorebook routing and embedding scans run, so keys can safely match real character/persona names even when the triggering text originally contained {{char}}/{{user}} macros; authors do not need keys targeting literal macro strings (#3704).

title: Missing 2.3.2 editor undo/redo and Tab indent restoration
reality: v2.3.2 restored native undo and redo in shared text editors including lorebook Content and Description fields, and made Tab / Shift+Tab indent or unindent every selected line without replacing the selection.
fix: Add to the 'Editor conveniences' subsection under UI Location: (v2.3.2) lorebook Content and Description editors support native undo/redo again, and Tab / Shift+Tab indents/unindents all selected lines (multi-line indent) instead of replacing the selection.

title: Missing Lorebook Prompt Position control
reality: v2.3.3 (#3733) references a 'Lorebook Prompt Position' native selector in the shared Lorebook editor shell (fixed to stay visually stable under Accent Pulse), i.e., a lorebook-level prompt-position control exists in the editor UI alongside the per-entry `position` field.
fix: In the UI Location / editor section (or near the per-entry `position` field docs), mention the lorebook editor's 'Lorebook Prompt Position' selector as the lorebook-level control governing where lorebook content sits in the prompt, distinct from per-entry `position` (0/1/2) overrides.

title: Missing Professor Mari atomic lorebook-entry saves fix
reality: v2.3.x (#3674) fixed Professor Mari returning blank character or lorebook generation turns and made her lorebook creation save generated entries atomically (no partial entry sets on failure).
fix: In the 'AI-assisted lorebook creation (Professor Mari)' section, add a note: generated entries are saved atomically (all-or-nothing), and the earlier blank-generation-turn bug is fixed — partial/blank lorebook drafts from Mari are no longer expected behavior worth working around.

title: Missing file-native storage and duplicate-link constraint change
reality: v2.3.0 removed the retired database compatibility stack — storage schemas are file-native throughout the Engine — and made file-native primary/natural-key constraints enforceable during atomic inserts and updates, preventing lorebook links (among others) from persisting ambiguous duplicates.
fix: Add a brief v2.3.0 note in the Scope or Character Lorebook tab section: lorebook links are now protected by file-native unique-key constraints, so the same lorebook can no longer end up ambiguously double-linked to a character/chat; duplicate-link states seen in older versions self-resolve and cannot recur.
